checks.item: start_year 1729: Kolachi-jo-Goth founded as a fortified trading settlement on Karachi harbour
checks.source_opened: https://archive.org/details/imperialgazettee15grea (full text, Karachi City article, pp. 11-17) ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karachi
checks.found: Gazetteer: 'Before 1725 no town whatever appears to have existed on the site ... a migration was made to a spot near the present head of Karachi harbour, and at that time (1729) called Kalachi Kun ... Cannon brought from Muscat protected the little fort'. Wikipedia: 'formally founded as the fortified village of Kolachi only in 1729'; 'A new settlement was built in 1729 ... known as Kolachi-jo-Goth'.
checks.detail: Year and description supported by both cited sources.

checks.found: Wikipedia: 'The population in 1856 is estimated to have been 57,000' (Heitzman 2008, p. 129). Search hit inside Heitzman: 'increased to about 57,000 by 1856'. The Wikipedia population table on the same page lists 22,227 for 1856 and 56,859 for 1861 from another source.
checks.detail: Heitzman states the figure. The differing table entry on Wikipedia comes from a different source and area, and the point is already marked estimated.

checks.found: Gazetteer: population '(1872) 56,753, (1881) 73,560, (1891) 105,199, and (1901) 116,663, of whom 8,019 resided in the cantonment' (OCR reads '73>56o'). The Wikipedia timeline gives 1881 as 68,332 town + 5,228 cantonment, which sums to 73,560.
checks.detail: Exact match; figure includes the cantonment.

checks.found: 'a very heterogeneous population of 151,903, as enumerated at the census of 1911. The municipal limits ... enclose an area of about seventy square miles.'
checks.detail: Number, year and area match the gazetteer.

checks.item: Empress Market: completed 1889, height 42.7 m, at 24.8625, 67.0294 (documented)
checks.found: Smyth: 'Empress Market ... opened in March 1891 ... In the front rises a massive tower 140 feet high'. Wikipedia: 'constructed between 1884 and 1889'; coordinates 24°51'45"N 67°1'46"E (24.8625, 67.0294).
checks.detail: 140 ft is 42.7 m; 1889 is the construction end date on Wikipedia and the 1891 opening date is already given in the note; coordinates match.

checks.item: Merewether Clock Tower: completed 1892, height 31.1 m, at 24.8489, 66.9974 (documented)
checks.found: Smyth: '[height] of 102 feet and carries, at an elevation of 70 feet, a clock with four faces ... foundation stone was laid ... in 1884, and the completed structure was opened ... in 1892'. Wikipedia: opened 1892, 31 m, coordinates 24°50.936'N 66°59.845'E (24.8489, 66.9974).
checks.detail: 102 ft is 31.1 m; year and coordinates match.

checks.found: 'the Manora breakwater, 1,503 feet in length - was commenced in 1869, and completed in 1873 at a cost of 7 lakhs. It affords complete shelter to the entrance channel (eastern) over the bar ... has already led to the deepening at the entrance'.
checks.detail: Length, dates and purpose match the gazetteer.

checks.item: 1878: Linked to the Indian railway network; by 1899 the largest wheat-exporting port in the East
checks.found: Wikipedia: 'In 1878, the British Raj connected Karachi with the network of British India's vast railway system' (Heitzman) and 'By 1899, Karachi had become the largest wheat-exporting port in the East' (cited there to Feldman 1970). Heitzman search hit: '[railways] linked to Karachi in 1878'.
checks.detail: Both statements are on the cited Wikipedia page; note the wheat sentence is referenced there to Feldman (1970), not Heitzman. Data left unchanged.

summary: All 10 sampled items matched the cited sources; the two gazetteers were read in full text on archive.org and Heitzman was checked through archive.org text search. Nothing was changed.
